inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K + Q2-FY2026 10-Q cash flow statements, TTM basis (FY2025 + H1-FY2026 - H1-FY2025): SBC add-back $2,029m plus $418m cash taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards. Adobe publishes no single combined figure, so per owner-fcf.md section 1(a) the two disclosed lines are summed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, Q2-FY2026 10-Q (2026-05-29). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count. Adobe is a heavy repurchaser ($11.28bn in FY2025, $4.59bn in H1-FY2026, with $50bn of authorizations running to 2028/2030 against a $116bn market cap), so the flat count is genuinely funded rather than a modelling convention. Actual count has fallen 485.5m (FY2020) to 402.5m.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted, per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing (operating company: application software / SaaS). Confirmed against the routing table rather than assumed.
BASE: FY0 is TTM (FY2025 + H1-FY2026 - H1-FY2025) = revenue $25,198m, reported FCF $10,280m, owner FCF $7,833m (30.9% margin vs 40.8% reported). The component build reproduces FY0 owner FCF at $7,637m (30.3%), 2.5% below actual, i.e. mildly conservative.
INTEREST INCOME NOT STRIPPED: Adobe holds NET DEBT of $1,726m, not net cash. Section 1(b) strips interest income only when net cash is added back to EV; here cash is netted against debt in the bridge, so the $264m of interest income is left in the flows and no double-count arises.
HORIZON: 10 years. Base owner-FCF margin is flat by year 5 (30.1%) but the bear case is still compressing through year 8, so capitalizing at year 5 would misstate the downside path.
WACC 9.5% USD, built from a 4.3% risk-free rate, 5.0% ERP and beta ~1.15 (CoE 10.05%) blended with after-tax cost of debt ~3.0% at 94.6/5.4 weights, giving 9.67%; rounded to 9.5%. Applied UNIFORMLY across scenarios so risk is charged once, in the flows, not twice (owner-fcf.md section 7f).
ARR: Digital Media ARR ($19.20bn FY2025) and Total Adobe ARR ($25.20bn FY2025, $27.10bn Q2-FY2026) are two different definitions after the FY2026 redefinition and are NEVER chained. Reported growth is ~10-11%, not 36%.
SEGMENTS: single reportable segment from FY2026, so FY2026 quarters carry no Digital Media / Digital Experience split.
LEADERSHIP: no permanent CEO named as of 2026-08-28 (Narayen announced departure March 2026) and an interim CFO since June 2026. Charged in the flows via the 30% bear weight, not via a WACC premium.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FLAGGED: equity CAGR is negative (-6.13% 3yr, -2.61% 5yr) against +10.52% revenue and +10.99% owner-FCF. This is a BUYBACK ARTIFACT, not deterioration: $11.28bn of FY2025 repurchases shrank book equity from $14.8bn (FY2021) to $11.5bn while revenue and cash flow compounded. Equity CAGR is therefore rejected as the growth driver and owner-FCF CAGR used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (10.99% 3yr / 14.87% 5yr) runs slightly ABOVE reported-FCF CAGR (10.03% / 13.17%), because SBC including equity-award taxes fell from 12.4% of revenue in FY2020 to 9.7% on a TTM basis. SBC is growing more slowly than cash flow -- the opposite of the usual warning sign. All CAGRs are computed on the consistently SBC-adjusted owner-FCF series.

base.description: Adobe grows into the low-to-mid single digits off the TTM base as the deliberate freemium pivot trades near-term ARR growth for funnel: FY2026 lands on the raised $26.50-26.60bn guidance (~5.5% off the $25.2bn TTM base, ~12% off FY2025 including roughly $480m of acquired Semrush ARR), reaccelerates modestly in FY2027-28 as paid conversion and AI-credit monetization begin to land, then fades to a 3% terminal. Adjusted EBITDA margin holds near management's ~45% non-GAAP operating-margin target plus D&A (48-49%), absorbing AI inference costs against subscription scale. SBC eases from 9.7% to 8.0% of revenue. The axes here are Creative Cloud pricing power against Canva/OpenAI substitution, and whether the 90M+ freemium MAU funnel converts before the legacy $20bn+ base erodes.

bull.description: The freemium bet pays off: AI-first ARR compounds off its $500m base, Firefly monetization scales, and paid conversion from the 90M+ creative freemium MAUs (growing 70%+ YoY) reaccelerates total growth to double digits from FY2027, exactly as management has guided investors to expect. Enterprise ($10m+ ARR) customers keep growing 20%+, GenStudio establishes the content supply chain as a category, and Semrush plus Topaz prove accretive. Operating leverage carries adjusted EBITDA margin to 52% while SBC falls to 7.5% of revenue. A permanent AI-native CEO is named and the leadership discount unwinds.

bear.description: The structural-decline case, which is what the market is actually pricing. Deferring the planned Creative Cloud price increases is treated as what it looks like: an admission that AI-native substitutes have become good enough to cap what Adobe can charge its professional base. Growth decelerates to roughly 1% by FY2028 and turns mildly negative as seats churn to Canva, Figma and generative tools, so revenue is lower in year 10 than in year 1. The freemium pivot plus AI compute permanently compresses adjusted EBITDA margin from 48% to 38%, and SBC RISES as a share of a shrinking top line because retention comp in a decline is sticky. The deferred-revenue tailwind collapses with growth. This is a genuine erosion path, not a haircut.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Flat cells at low WACC / high terminal growth are the 17x terminal cap binding (TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 17x FCF_10))), which is the intended behaviour: it stops a small terminal-growth change from running the valuation away.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Deliberately NOT the 15/50/35 house default. Bear is raised to 30% and bull cut to 20% because the bear case here is structural rather than cyclical, and three independent things would each have to go right for the bull: freemium conversion at scale, Firefly monetization outrunning substitution, and a successful CEO transition. Adobe has two unresolved leadership vacancies (no permanent CEO five months after the March 2026 announcement; interim CFO), has itself deferred planned Creative Cloud price increases, and AI-first ARR is still under 2% of the ~$27bn base -- so the disruption risk is immediate and already visible while the offset is unproven. Offsetting that, ~96-97% subscription revenue, $10bn+ of annual cash generation and an investment-grade balance sheet mean the bear case is margin and growth erosion, NOT solvency, which is why bear stays at 30% rather than higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: Band position is NEGATIVE (-40%), which is the finding: the market is paying less than the fully-SBC-expensed house value, i.e. below the floor of the accounting-regime band rather than somewhere inside it. On the street convention (SBC as non-cash) the weighted value is $427.87.

valuation_philosophy.model: Owner-FCF DCF, three scenarios, probability-weighted, 10-year explicit horizon
valuation_philosophy.basis: House basis expenses SBC in full (including cash taxes paid on net-share settlement) and holds the diluted share count FLAT, so grant dilution is charged exactly once. Street basis, reported alongside, adds back the PV of that SBC charge.
valuation_philosophy.why_this_model: Adobe is a ~96-97% subscription operating company with durable positive free cash flow, so the routing table in dcf-methods/SKILL.md sends it to owner-FCF. The non-FCF models exist for businesses whose cash flow statements do not mean what this engine assumes -- banks, REITs, LICs, distressed shells -- none of which describes Adobe.
key_judgments: FY0 is TTM, not FY2025, so the base reflects H1-FY2026 including Semrush.
Margins are built from components each year (EBITDA -> SBC -> D&A -> tax -> capex -> working capital); the latest FCF margin is never carried forward flat.

Working capital is modelled as a capture rate on the CHANGE in revenue, because the deferred-revenue inflow is a function of bookings growth and shrinks hard when growth decelerates -- a 5-year average of 29% of the revenue increase, taken at 25% in base.
Interest income is left in the flows because Adobe carries net debt; stripping it would be the mirror-image error of double-counting a cash pile that is not there.
The terminal cap is 17x base / 20x bull / 12x bear, justified from the DE-RATED recent range rather than the FY2020-21 bubble multiples.
Risk is charged once, in the scenario weights and flows -- a single 9.5% WACC across all three scenarios.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_it: Q3-FY2026 net-new Digital Media ARR (due mid-September 2026), which management has pre-warned will look soft by design; a permanent CEO appointment; and evidence on whether freemium MAUs convert to paid at a rate that offsets deferred pricing.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted (house) TTM per-share metrics: EPS $11.88, owner FCF $19.46, book value $28.62, revenue $62.60
sanity_check.diagnosis:
PASS, and this is the INVERSE of the usual failure mode. The check exists to catch a DCF implying multiples the market has never paid (the SEK.NZ failure). Here every scenario implies multiples BELOW Adobe's own 10-year history: base IV $360.99 implies 30.4x SBC-adjusted P/E against a 10-year average of 62.3x, median 63.2x and minimum 26.3x; 12.1x EV/EBITDA against a 42.7x average and 18.1x minimum. The bull case at 43.3x P/E still sits below the 10-year average. So the model does not require any re-rating toward the FY2020-21 bubble multiples -- those years (85.9x in FY2021) are explicitly treated as the outliers, and the 17x terminal FCF cap was set from the de-rated recent range, not the long-run average.
The genuine risk to be honest about runs the other way: the multiple has ALREADY compressed to the bottom of its decade range (24.3x SBC-adjusted P/E, 9.7x EV/EBITDA versus an 18.1x historical minimum), because the market is pricing real AI-substitution risk. A DCF that simply extrapolated 11% growth would show enormous upside and would be answering the wrong question. That is why the bear case is a structural-decline path -- growth to ~1% then negative, revenue LOWER in year 10 than year 1, margin from 48% to 38%, SBC rising as a share of a shrinking top line -- rather than a mild haircut, and why it carries a 30% weight. At $152.46 the bear case is -47% from today, so the weighted +13.8% upside is a genuinely contested call, not a layup.

prior_version.price_basis: last refreshed 2026-08-12 at $263.71 over a 2026-06-30 model

reconciliation.nature_of_change: METHODOLOGY REBUILD, not a driver refresh. The prior DCF predates this repo's owner-FCF policy: it valued Adobe on reported FCF with SBC treated as non-cash, carried a FLAT 41.45% FCF margin forward instead of building margins from components, ran a 5-year horizon, used a stale 397.5m share count, and computed the entry price as terminal-value-per-share discounted at 15% (the formula corrected on 2026-07-21, which the memory notes made entry prices 40-50% too low). Every scenario driver has therefore been re-judged deliberately, which is the exception to the usual do-not-re-derive rule and is stated here explicitly.

bridge.item: Reweight to 30/50/20 for unresolved CEO/CFO vacancies and structural (not cyclical) bear case
New driver paths, 10-year horizon, TTM base, component margin build, refreshed 402.5m share count -- measured on the STREET basis so it is comparable with the prior SBC-as-non-cash treatment
bridge.note: Small: the prior flat-margin model and the new component build happen to land close on a pre-SBC basis.

bridge.item: SBC expensed in full (incl. $418m cash taxes on net-share settlement), share count held flat -- the house owner-FCF policy the prior version did not apply
bridge.note: This single policy change is the overwhelming driver of the decline. It is a change in what is being measured, not a deterioration in Adobe.

price_move.note: Price moved +5.0%; this affects upside percentages, not intrinsic value.

unchanged_and_why.note: Now built explicitly from a USD CAPM (4.3% rf, 5.0% ERP, beta 1.15 => 9.67%) and applied UNIFORMLY, because the prior model's per-scenario WACC spread charged risk twice -- once in the flows and again in the discount rate. Would move on a material change in the risk-free rate or Adobe's beta.
Still consistent with long-run nominal GDP for a dominant subscription platform. Bear cut to 1.0% to match a genuinely eroding business; bull 3.5%.

Same Q2-FY2026 (2026-05-29) balance sheet as the prior version -- $6,645m debt less $4,919m cash. Would move on the Q3-FY2026 10-Q, especially given continued buybacks and the Semrush/Topaz cash outlays.
